title.zh: 卷一 補帝紀第一 神武帝上
title.raw: 卷一 補帝紀第一 神武帝上 Volume 1 Annals 1: Emperor Shenwu 1

sentences.zh: 神武上

translations.literal: Emperor Shenwu, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenwu, Part One

sentences.zh: 齊高祖神武皇帝，姓高名歡，字賀六渾，渤海蓚人也。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor of Qi, Emperor Shenwu, surname Gao, taboo name Huan, style name Heiliuhun, was a native of Tiao in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenwu, posthumous temple name Gaozu of Northern Qi, bore the surname Gao; his personal name was Huan and his style Heiliuhun. He came from Tiao in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 六世祖隱，晉玄菟太守。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Yin served as Administrator of Xuantu under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth generation his ancestor Yin had been Administrator of Xuantu under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 隱生慶，慶生泰，泰生湖，三世仕慕容氏。

translations.literal: Yin begot Qing; Qing begot Tai; Tai begot Hu — three generations served the Murong house.
translations.idiomatic: Yin fathered Qing, Qing fathered Tai, and Tai fathered Hu; all three generations entered the service of the Murong clan.

sentences.zh: 及慕容寶敗，國亂，湖率衆歸魏，為右將軍。

translations.literal: When Murong Bao was defeated and the realm fell into chaos, Hu led his followers to submit to Wei and was made Right General.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Bao suffered defeat and the state collapsed into disorder, Hu brought his band over to the Northern Wei and was appointed Right General.

sentences.zh: 湖生四子，第三子謐，仕魏，位至侍御史，坐法徙居懷朔鎮。

translations.literal: Hu had four sons; the third, Mi, served Wei, rose to Attending Censor, and for violating the law was exiled to garrison at Huaishuo.
translations.idiomatic: Hu had four sons. The third, Mi, served the Wei court and rose to Attending Censor, but after a legal infraction was banished to live at Huaishuo garrison.

sentences.zh: 謐生皇考樹，性通率，不事家業。

translations.literal: Mi begot the late father Shu, who by nature was frank and unassuming and did not attend to the family occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Mi fathered Gao Huan's father Shu, a man frank and easy in temperament who cared little for the family trade.

sentences.zh: 住居白道南，數有赤光紫氣之異，鄰人以為怪，勸徙居以避之。

translations.literal: He lived south of the White Road; repeatedly there were portents of red light and purple vapor, and neighbors, deeming it strange, urged him to move away to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: He lived south of the White Road, where red light and purple vapors appeared again and again. The neighbors took this for uncanny and urged him to move elsewhere to escape it.

sentences.zh: 皇考曰：「安知非吉？

translations.literal: The late father said: "Who is to say it is not auspicious?
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan's father replied, "How do you know it is not a blessing?

sentences.zh: 」居之自若。

translations.literal: " He remained there as before.
translations.idiomatic: And he stayed on as before, unperturbed.

sentences.zh: 及神武生而皇妣韓氏殂，養於同產姊婿鎮獄隊尉景家。

translations.literal: When Shenwu was born the late mother Lady Han died, and he was raised in the home of his uterine elder sister's husband, Jing, captain of the garrison prison guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan was born his mother Lady Han died, and he was reared in the household of his full elder sister's husband Jing, captain of the garrison prison guard.

sentences.zh: 神武旣累世北邊，故習其俗，遂同鮮卑。

translations.literal: As for generations his family had been on the northern frontier, Shenwu was accustomed to its customs and came to be as the Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had lived on the northern marches, so Gao Huan grew up in frontier ways and lived much like the Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 長而深沉有大度，輕財重士，為豪俠所宗。

translations.literal: When grown he was deep and reserved, possessed of great breadth of mind, lightly regarded wealth and valued men of talent, and was looked to by bold heroes.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he was reserved and far-sighted, generous with money and devoted to worthy companions, and the local men of daring looked to him as their leader.

sentences.zh: 目有精光，長頭高顴，齒白如玉，少有人傑表。

translations.literal: His eyes had a sharp brilliance; his head was long and cheeks high; his teeth white as jade — in youth he had the countenance of an uncommon man.
translations.idiomatic: His eyes gleamed, his head was long and his cheekbones high, his teeth white as jade; even in youth he wore the bearing of a man marked for greatness.

sentences.zh: 家貧，及聘武明皇后，始有馬，得給鎮為隊主。

translations.literal: His family was poor; only when he betrothed Empress Wuming did he first have a horse and was able to serve the garrison as squad chief.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor, and only after he betrothed Lady Wuming did he acquire a horse and win appointment as squad chief at the garrison.

sentences.zh: 鎮將遼西段長常奇神武貌，謂曰：「君有康濟才，終不徒然。

translations.literal: Duan Chang of Liaoxi, commander of the garrison, often marveled at Shenwu's appearance and said to him: "You possess talent for bringing order and succor; you will not in the end come to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Chang of Liaoxi, the garrison commander, often admired Gao Huan's looks and told him, "You have the talent to heal the realm; you will not end your days obscurely.

sentences.zh: 」便以子孫為托。

translations.literal: " He thereupon entrusted him with his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: And he entrusted his descendants to Gao Huan's care.

sentences.zh: 及貴，追贈長司空，擢其子寧用之。

translations.literal: When Shenwu rose high, he posthumously enfeoffed Chang as Minister of Works and promoted his son Ning to employment.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao Huan rose to power he posthumously enfeoffed Duan Chang as Minister of Works and brought his son Ning into office.

sentences.zh: 神武自隊主轉為函使。

translations.literal: Shenwu advanced from squad chief to courier.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan moved from squad chief to garrison courier.

sentences.zh: 嘗乘驛過建興，雲霧晝晦，雷聲隨之，半日乃絕，若有神應者。

translations.literal: Once riding post through Jianxing, clouds and mist darkened the day, thunder followed along, and for half a day it did not cease — as if there were a divine response.
translations.idiomatic: Once while riding post through Jianxing, clouds and mist darkened the day and thunder rolled after him for half a day, as though heaven itself were answering his passage.

sentences.zh: 每行道路，往來無風塵之色。

translations.literal: Whenever he traveled the roads, there was no look of wind and dust about his coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he traveled the roads he seemed untouched by wind and dust.

sentences.zh: 又嘗夢履衆星而行，覺而內喜。

translations.literal: Again he once dreamed of treading among the stars as he walked; waking, he rejoiced inwardly.
translations.idiomatic: He also dreamed once that he walked treading upon the stars; when he woke he was secretly elated.

sentences.zh: 為函使六年，每至洛陽，給令史麻祥使。

translations.literal: For six years as courier, whenever he reached Luoyang he was detailed to the clerk Ma Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: For six years as courier he went each time to Luoyang, where he was assigned to the clerk Ma Xiang.

sentences.zh: 詳嘗以肉啖神武，神武性不立食，坐而進之。

translations.literal: Xiang once offered meat to Shenwu to eat; Shenwu by nature would not eat standing, and so sat to receive it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang once fed him meat; Gao Huan, who never ate standing, sat down to accept it.

sentences.zh: 祥以為慢己，笞神武四十。

translations.literal: Xiang took this as disrespect toward himself and had Shenwu flogged forty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang took this as an insult and had Gao Huan beaten forty strokes.

sentences.zh: 及自洛陽還，傾產以結客。

translations.literal: When he returned from Luoyang, he expended his whole estate to gather clients.
translations.idiomatic: On his return from Luoyang he poured out his fortune to gather followers.

sentences.zh: 親故怪問之，答曰：「吾至洛陽，宿衛羽林相率焚領軍張彝宅，朝廷懼其亂而不問。

translations.literal: Relatives and friends wondered and asked him; he replied: "When I reached Luoyang, the palace guards of the Feathered Forest together burned the residence of the supreme commander Zhang Yi, and the court feared their disorder and did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Kinsmen and friends asked what moved him; he answered, "At Luoyang I saw the Feathered Forest guards burn down the residence of Supreme Commander Zhang Yi in a mob, and the court, fearing worse trouble, never punished them.

sentences.zh: 為政若此，事可知也。

translations.literal: When government is like this, how affairs will turn out is plain to see.
translations.idiomatic: When government runs thus, the course of events is already clear.

sentences.zh: 財物豈可常守邪？

translations.literal: Can wealth and goods be kept forever?
translations.idiomatic: What good is clinging to property forever?

sentences.zh: 」自是乃有澄清天下之志。

translations.literal: " From this time he nursed the ambition to cleanse and clarify the realm.
translations.idiomatic: From that day he resolved to set the realm right.

sentences.zh: 與懷朔省事雲中司馬子如及秀容人劉貴、中山人賈顯智為奔走之友，懷朔戶曹史孫騰、外兵史侯景亦相友結。

translations.literal: With Sima Ziru, affairs clerk of Yunzhong at Huaishuo, Liu Gui of Xiurong, and Jia Xianzhi of Zhongshan he formed a band of comrades ready to run errands; Sun Teng, household clerk at Huaishuo, and Hou Jing, clerk in external military affairs, also joined in friendship.
translations.idiomatic: He made running companions of Sima Ziru, affairs clerk at Huaishuo's Yunzhong desk, Liu Gui of Xiurong, and Jia Xianzhi of Zhongshan; Sun Teng, the garrison household clerk, and Hou Jing, clerk for external military affairs, joined their circle as well.

sentences.zh: 劉貴嘗得一白鷹，與神武及尉景、蔡儁、子如、賈顯智等獵於沃野。

translations.literal: Liu Gui once obtained a white hawk and hunted on the open fields with Shenwu, Jing, Cai Jun, Ziru, Jia Xianzhi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gui once came by a white hawk and went hunting on the open steppe with Gao Huan, Jing, Cai Jun, Ziru, Jia Xianzhi, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 見一赤兔，每搏輒逸，遂至回澤。

translations.literal: They saw a red hare; each time they closed in it escaped, and they went on as far as Huize Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: They sighted a russet hare that bolted away whenever they closed, and the chase carried them to Huize Marsh.

sentences.zh: 澤中有茅屋，將奔入，有狗自屋中出，噬之，鷹兔俱死。

translations.literal: In the marsh there was a thatched hut; as the hare was about to flee into it, a dog came out from the hut and bit it, and hawk and hare both died.
translations.idiomatic: Near a hut on the marsh the hare was nearly inside when a dog rushed out, tore at it, and killed both hawk and hare.

sentences.zh: 神武怒，以鳴鏑射之，狗斃。

translations.literal: Shenwu in anger shot it with a whistling arrow and killed the dog.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan, furious, killed the dog with a whistling arrow.

sentences.zh: 屋中有二人出，持神武襟甚急。

translations.literal: Two men came out from the hut and seized Shenwu's robe with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Two men burst from the hut and seized Gao Huan's robe in alarm.

sentences.zh: 其母兩目盲，曳杖呵其二子曰：「何故觸大家！

translations.literal: Their mother, blind in both eyes, dragged her staff and rebuked her two sons, saying: "Why do you offend the great lord!
translations.idiomatic: Their blind mother, leaning on her staff, scolded them: "Why do you lay hands on our great guest!

sentences.zh: 」出甕中酒，烹羊以飯客。

translations.literal: " She brought out wine from a jar, cooked sheep, and fed the guests.
translations.idiomatic: She brought wine from a jar, slaughtered a sheep, and feasted them.

sentences.zh: 因自言善暗相，遍捫諸人皆貴，而指麾俱由神武。

translations.literal: She then said herself that she was skilled at reading fortune by touch; she felt over everyone and found them all noble, yet all destinies depended on Shenwu's direction.
translations.idiomatic: Declaring herself skilled in reading fate by touch, she passed her hands over each man and pronounced them all destined for rank, yet said every fortune turned on Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「子如歷位顯，智不善終。

translations.literal: She also said: "Ziru will achieve distinguished rank, but Zhi will not end well.
translations.idiomatic: She added, "Ziru will rise to high office, but Xianzhi will meet an ill end.

sentences.zh: 」飯竟出，行數里還，更訪之，則本無人居，乃向非人也。

translations.literal: " When the meal was done they left; after going several li they turned back to visit again, but where there had been no dwelling at all — those before had not been human.
translations.idiomatic: After the meal they rode on, but a few li later turned back to find the place, and there was no hut at all—their hosts had not been of this world.

sentences.zh: 由是諸人益加敬異。

translations.literal: From this the company all the more revered and marvelled at him.
translations.idiomatic: From that day his companions held him in still greater awe.

sentences.zh: 孝昌元年，柔玄鎮人杜洛周反於上谷，神武乃與同志從之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaochang, Du Luozhou of Rouxuan garrison rebelled at Shanggu, and Shenwu with his like-minded comrades followed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiaochang (525), Du Luozhou of Rouxuan garrison rebelled at Shanggu, and Gao Huan and his companions joined him.

sentences.zh: 醜其行事，私與尉景、段榮、蔡儁圖之。

translations.literal: He loathed Luozhou's conduct and secretly with Jing, Duan Rong, and Cai Jun plotted against him.
translations.idiomatic: Disgusted by Luozhou's methods, he secretly plotted with Jing, Duan Rong, and Cai Jun.

sentences.zh: 不果而逃，為其騎所追。

translations.literal: The plot did not succeed and he fled; Luozhou's cavalry pursued him.
translations.idiomatic: The plot failed and he fled, with Luozhou's horsemen in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 文襄及魏永熙后皆幼，武明後於牛上抱負之。

translations.literal: Wenxiang and the Empress Dowager of Yongxi of Wei were both young; Empress Wuming on the ox bore them in her arms.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang and the future Empress Yongxi of Wei were still small children; Empress Wuming carried them on the ox in her arms.

sentences.zh: 文襄屢落牛，神武彎弓將射之以決去。

translations.literal: Wenxiang repeatedly fell from the ox; Shenwu bent his bow intending to shoot him to settle whether to go on.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang kept falling from the ox; Gao Huan strung his bow as if to shoot the boy dead and be rid of the burden.

sentences.zh: 后呼榮求救，賴榮遽下取之以免。

translations.literal: The empress called to Rong for rescue; thanks to Rong quickly descending to take him up, he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wuming cried to Duan Rong for help, and Rong leapt down in time to catch the boy and save him.

sentences.zh: 遂奔葛榮，又亡歸尒朱榮於秀容。

translations.literal: He then fled to Ge Rong, and again broke away and returned to Erzhu Rong at Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: He fled next to Ge Rong, then broke away again and took refuge with Erzhu Rong at Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 先是，劉貴事榮，盛言神武美，至是始得見，以憔悴故，未之奇也。

translations.literal: Earlier Liu Gui had served Rong and lavishly praised Shenwu's excellence; only now did he first gain an audience, but because he was haggard, Rong did not regard him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gui had long served Erzhu Rong and spoken lavishly of Gao Huan's gifts; now Gao Huan finally met Rong face to face, but worn and haggard as he was, Rong saw nothing remarkable in him.

sentences.zh: 貴乃為神武更衣，復求見焉。

translations.literal: Gui then changed Shenwu's clothing and sought another audience.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gui dressed Gao Huan in fresh clothes and arranged another meeting.

sentences.zh: 因隨榮之廄。

translations.literal: Thereupon he followed Rong to the stables.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Rong into the stables.

sentences.zh: 廄有惡馬，榮命翦之。

translations.literal: In the stable there was a vicious horse; Rong ordered its mane clipped.
translations.idiomatic: A vicious stallion was in the stable, and Rong ordered its mane clipped.

sentences.zh: 神武乃不加羈絆而翦，竟不蹄齧，已而起曰：「御惡人亦如此馬矣。

translations.literal: Shenwu then clipped it without adding halter or tie, and in the end it did not kick or bite; when done he rose and said: "Handling wicked men is also like this horse.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan clipped it without halter or hobble, and the beast never kicked or bit; when he finished he stood and said, "Taming wicked men is like taming this horse.

sentences.zh: 」榮遂坐神武於床下，屏左右而訪時事。

translations.literal: " Rong thereupon seated Shenwu below his couch, dismissed those on either side, and inquired about current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Rong then seated Gao Huan below his couch, dismissed his attendants, and questioned him on the state of the realm.

sentences.zh: 神武曰：「聞公有馬十二谷，色別為羣，將此竟何用也？

translations.literal: Shenwu said: "I hear you have horses in twelve valleys, grouped by color — to what end do you keep them all?
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan asked, "I hear you pasture horses in twelve valleys, sorted by color—what do you mean to do with them?

sentences.zh: 」榮曰：「但言爾意。

translations.literal: " Rong said: "Just speak your mind.
translations.idiomatic: Rong replied, "Tell me what you have in mind.

sentences.zh: 」神武曰：「方今天子愚弱，太后淫亂，孽寵擅命，朝政不行。

translations.literal: " Shenwu said: "At present the Son of Heaven is foolish and weak, the Empress Dowager debauched and disorderly, favorite minions hold command at will, and court governance does not function.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "The emperor is weak and the empress dowager debauched; favored creatures command at will and the court has ceased to govern.

sentences.zh: 以明公雄武，乘時奮發，討鄭儼、徐紇而清帝側，霸業可舉鞭而成。

translations.literal: With your heroic martial power, sir, if you seize the moment and strike, punish Zheng Yan and Xu He and cleanse the emperor's side — hegemony can be achieved at a flick of the whip.
translations.idiomatic: With your might, my lord, rise now, strike down Zheng Yan and Xu He, cleanse the emperor's side—and dominion over the realm is yours at a flick of the whip.

sentences.zh: 此賀六渾之意也。

translations.literal: This is Heiliuhun's intent.
translations.idiomatic: That is Heiliuhun's counsel.

sentences.zh: 」榮大悅，語自日中至夜半，乃出。

translations.literal: " Rong was greatly pleased; they spoke from midday until midnight before he departed.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was delighted; they talked from noon until midnight before Gao Huan left.

sentences.zh: 自是每參軍謀。

translations.literal: From this time he took part in every military council.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Gao Huan was included in every council of war.

sentences.zh: 後從榮徙據幷州，抵揚州邑人龐蒼鷹，止團焦中。

translations.literal: Later following Rong he moved to hold Bing Province, arrived at Pang Cangying of Yangzhou township, and lodged in a round walled compound.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Rong shifted his base to Bing Province, Gao Huan stayed with Pang Cangying of Yangzhou township in a round-walled compound called Tuanjiao.

sentences.zh: 每從外歸，主人遙聞行響動地。

translations.literal: Whenever he returned from outside, the host from afar heard his footsteps shaking the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Gao Huan returned from outside, his host heard from far off footsteps that seemed to shake the earth.

sentences.zh: 蒼鷹母數見團焦赤氣赫然屬天。

translations.literal: Cangying's mother often saw over the compound a red vapor blazing up to the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Cangying's mother often saw over the compound a scarlet aura blazing up to heaven.

sentences.zh: 又蒼鷹嘗夜欲入，有青衣人拔刀叱曰：「何故觸王！

translations.literal: Again Cangying once at night wished to enter; a man in blue robes drew a sword and shouted: "Why do you offend the king!
translations.idiomatic: One night Cangying tried to enter and a man in blue robes drew a sword and cried, "How dare you disturb the king!

sentences.zh: 」言訖不見。

translations.literal: " When the words ended he was not to be seen.
translations.idiomatic: When he finished speaking, the figure vanished.

sentences.zh: 始以為異，密覘之，唯見赤蛇蟠床上，乃益驚異。

translations.literal: At first taking it for strange, he secretly watched and saw only a red serpent coiled on the bed; he was all the more startled and marveled.
translations.idiomatic: At first puzzled, he stole a look inside and saw only a red serpent coiled on the bed; his wonder only grew.

sentences.zh: 因殺牛分肉，厚以相奉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he slaughtered an ox and divided the meat, generously presenting it to him.
translations.idiomatic: He slaughtered an ox and brought Gao Huan generous gifts of meat.

sentences.zh: 蒼鷹母求以神武為義子。

translations.literal: Cangying's mother asked to take Shenwu as an adopted son.
translations.idiomatic: Cangying's mother asked to adopt Gao Huan as a son.

sentences.zh: 及得志，以其宅為第，號為南宅。

translations.literal: When he achieved his ambition he made that dwelling his mansion, called the Southern Residence.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao Huan rose to power he made the house his own mansion and called it the Southern Residence.

sentences.zh: 雖門巷開廣，堂宇崇麗，其本所住團焦，以石堊塗之，留而不毀，至文宣時，遂為宮。

translations.literal: Although gateways and lanes were broadened and halls lofty and splendid, the original Tuanjiao where he had lived he plastered with stone and lime, preserving it undestroyed; by the time of Emperor Wenxuan it became a palace.
translations.idiomatic: Though his new halls grew wide and grand, he left the original Tuanjiao compound plastered in whitewashed stone, never torn down; under Emperor Wenxuan it became a palace.

sentences.zh: 旣而榮以神武為親信都督。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Rong made Shenwu trusted commander.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Erzhu Rong appointed Gao Huan trusted commander.

sentences.zh: 于於時魏明帝銜鄭儼、徐紇，逼靈太后，未敢制，私使榮舉兵內向。

translations.literal: At this time Wei Emperor Ming bore hatred for Zheng Yan and Xu He, who pressed the Empress Dowager Ling; he dared not restrain them and secretly sent Rong to raise troops inward.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Ming of Northern Wei loathed Zheng Yan and Xu He, who dominated Empress Dowager Ling, but dared not move against them openly; he secretly urged Erzhu Rong to march on the capital.

sentences.zh: 榮以神武為前鋒。

translations.literal: Rong made Shenwu vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Rong made Gao Huan his vanguard.

sentences.zh: 至上黨，明帝又私詔停之。

translations.literal: Reaching Shangdang, Ming again privately ordered him to halt.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Shangdang, the emperor secretly ordered a halt.

sentences.zh: 及帝暴崩，榮遂入洛，因將篡位。

translations.literal: When the emperor suddenly died, Rong then entered Luoyang and intended to usurp the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died suddenly, Rong entered Luoyang and prepared to seize the throne himself.

sentences.zh: 神武諫，恐不聽，請鑄像卜之，鑄不成，乃止。

translations.literal: Shenwu remonstrated; fearing he would not listen, he asked to cast an image and divined by it; the casting did not succeed, and so Rong stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan remonstrated; fearing Rong would not heed him, he had a Buddha image cast for divination—and when the casting failed, Rong abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 孝莊帝立，以定策勳，封銅鞮伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang was enthroned, for merit in settling the plan he was enfeoffed as Baron of Tongdi.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang took the throne, Gao Huan was enfeoffed Baron of Tongdi for his role in the settlement.

sentences.zh: 及尒朱榮擊葛榮，令神武喻下賊別稱王者七人。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong attacked Ge Rong, he had Shenwu persuade seven bandit chiefs styling themselves kings to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong campaigned against Ge Rong, he sent Gao Huan to talk seven rebel kings into surrender.

sentences.zh: 後與行臺于暉破羊侃於泰山，尋與元天穆破邢杲于濟南。

translations.literal: Later with Mobile Headquarters Yu Hui he defeated Yang Kan at Mount Tai; soon with Yuan Tianmu he defeated Xing Gao at Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined Mobile Headquarters Commander Yu Hui to defeat Yang Kan at Mount Tai, and soon after joined Yuan Tianmu to crush Xing Gao at Jinan.

sentences.zh: 累遷第三鎮人酋長，常在榮帳內。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to chief of the third garrison populations and was constantly within Rong's tent.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to become chief of the third garrison peoples and remained constantly at Erzhu Rong's side.

sentences.zh: 榮嘗問左右曰：「一日無我，誰可主軍？

translations.literal: Rong once asked those beside him: "One day without me — who could command the army?
translations.idiomatic: Rong once asked his companions, "If I were gone, who could lead these armies?

sentences.zh: 」皆稱尒朱兆。

translations.literal: " All named Erzhu Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: All named Erzhu Zhao.

sentences.zh: 曰：「此正可統三千騎以還，堪代我主衆者，唯賀六渾耳。

translations.literal: He said: "This one can just lead three thousand cavalry back; the man fit to replace me in commanding the masses is only Heiliuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "Zhao can lead three thousand horsemen home, but only Heiliuhun is fit to replace me in command of the host.

sentences.zh: 」因誡兆曰：「爾非其匹，終當為其穿鼻。

translations.literal: He thereupon warned Zhao: "You are not his match; in the end you will be bridled by him.
translations.idiomatic: He warned Zhao, "You are no match for him; in the end he will put the ring in your nose.

sentences.zh: 」乃以神武為晉州刺史。

translations.literal: " He then made Shenwu Inspector of Jin Province.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon appointed Gao Huan inspector of Jin Province.

sentences.zh: 於是大聚斂，因劉貴貨榮下要人，盡得其意。

translations.literal: Thereupon he greatly gathered riches; through Liu Gui he bribed Rong's key men and came fully to know their intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan amassed wealth on a grand scale and, through Liu Gui, bought off Erzhu Rong's inner circle until he knew their minds completely.

sentences.zh: 時州庫角無故自鳴，神武異之，無幾而孝莊誅榮。

translations.literal: At the time the horn of the provincial storehouse spontaneously sounded without cause; Shenwu took it as strange; before long Xiaozhuang executed Rong.
translations.idiomatic: About then a horn in the provincial storehouse sounded of its own accord; Gao Huan took it for an omen—and soon Emperor Xiaozhuang killed Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 及尒朱兆自晉陽將舉兵赴洛，召神武。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao from Jinyang was about to raise troops and march to Luoyang, he summoned Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao prepared to march from Jinyang on Luoyang, he summoned Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 神武使長史孫騰辭以絳蜀、汾胡欲反，不可委去。

translations.literal: Shenwu sent chief clerk Sun Teng to decline, citing that Jiang-Shu and Fen-Hu wished to rebel and he could not leave his post.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan sent his chief clerk Sun Teng to excuse him, claiming the Jiang-Shu and Fen-Hu tribes were on the verge of revolt and he could not abandon his post.

sentences.zh: 兆恨焉。

translations.literal: Zhao bore resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao resented the refusal.

sentences.zh: 騰復命，神武曰：「兆舉兵犯上，此大賊也，吾不能久事之。

translations.literal: Teng reported back; Shenwu said: "Zhao raises troops against his sovereign — this is a great rebel; I cannot serve him long.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Teng returned, Gao Huan said, "Zhao is marching against the throne—he is a traitor, and I cannot serve him much longer.

sentences.zh: 」自是始有圖兆計。

translations.literal: " From this time he first formed a plan against Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: From that moment he began plotting against Erzhu Zhao.

sentences.zh: 及兆入洛，執莊帝以北，神武聞之，大驚。

translations.literal: When Zhao entered Luoyang and took Emperor Zhuang north as prisoner, Shenwu heard and was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao entered Luoyang and dragged Emperor Xiaozhuang north as a prisoner, Gao Huan was dismayed.

sentences.zh: 又使孫騰偽賀兆，因密覘孝莊所在，將劫以舉義，不果。

translations.literal: Again he sent Sun Teng to feign congratulations to Zhao, and thereby secretly spy out where Xiaozhuang was, intending to seize him and raise a righteous army — it did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Sun Teng to offer Zhao false congratulations while secretly seeking Emperor Xiaozhuang's whereabouts, intending to rescue him and raise the banner of revolt—but the plan failed.

sentences.zh: 乃以書喻之，言不宜執天子以受惡名於海內。

translations.literal: He then wrote advising Zhao, saying it was not fitting to hold the Son of Heaven and thereby incur evil reputation throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote urging Zhao that holding the emperor captive would earn him infamy throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 兆不納，殺帝，而與尒朱世隆等立長廣王曄，改元建明。

translations.literal: Zhao did not accept; he killed the emperor, and with Erzhu Shilong and others enthroned Prince Changguang Ye and changed the era name to Jianming.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao refused heed, killed the emperor, and with Erzhu Shilong and others enthroned Prince Changguang of Changguang, changing the era name to Jianming.

sentences.zh: 封神武為平陽郡公。

translations.literal: Shenwu was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was enfeoffed Duke of Pingyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 及費也頭紇豆陵步藩入秀容，逼晉陽，兆徵神武。

translations.literal: When the Feiyetou tribe Helouling Bofan entered Xiurong and pressed Jinyang, Zhao summoned Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: When Helouling Bofan of the Feiyetou entered Xiurong and threatened Jinyang, Zhao again summoned Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 神武將往，賀拔焉過兒請緩行以弊之。

translations.literal: Shenwu was about to go; Heba Yanguo'er asked to delay the march to exhaust them.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was preparing to march when Heba Yanguo'er urged him to go slowly and wear the enemy down.

sentences.zh: 神武乃往往逗遛，辭以河無橋不得渡。

translations.literal: Shenwu then often dawdled, pleading that without a bridge over the river he could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan deliberately lingered, claiming there was no bridge and he could not cross the river.

sentences.zh: 步藩軍盛，兆敗走。

translations.literal: Bu Fan's army was strong; Zhao was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Fan's forces grew overwhelming and Erzhu Zhao was beaten and fled.

sentences.zh: 初，孝莊之誅尒朱榮，知其黨必有逆謀，乃密敕步藩令襲其後。

translations.literal: Initially, when Xiaozhuang executed Erzhu Rong, knowing his faction would surely harbor treasonous designs, he secretly ordered Bu Fan to strike their rear.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Xiaozhuang killed Erzhu Rong, he knew the Erzhu faction would rebel and secretly ordered Bu Fan to attack them from the rear.

sentences.zh: 步藩旣敗兆等，以兵勢日盛，兆又請救於神武。

translations.literal: After Bu Fan had defeated Zhao and the others, as his military strength daily grew, Zhao again asked Shenwu for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Once Bu Fan had routed Erzhu Zhao, his army grew stronger by the day, and Zhao turned again to Gao Huan for help.

sentences.zh: 神武內圖兆，復慮步藩後之難除，乃與兆悉力破之。

translations.literal: Shenwu inwardly plotted against Zhao, yet also feared that if Bu Fan were left later he would be hard to eliminate; he therefore joined Zhao with full force to break him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan intended to destroy Zhao but feared Bu Fan would prove still harder to remove later, so he joined Zhao and broke Bu Fan between them.

sentences.zh: 藩死，深德神武，誓為兄弟。

translations.literal: When Fan died, Zhao deeply felt gratitude toward Shenwu and swore brotherhood.
translations.idiomatic: After Bu Fan fell, Erzhu Zhao was deeply grateful to Gao Huan and swore brotherhood with him.

sentences.zh: 時世隆、度律、彥伯共執朝政，天光據關右，兆據幷州，仲遠據東郡，各擁兵為暴，天下苦之。

translations.literal: At that time Shilong, Dulü, and Yanbo jointly wielded court governance; Tianguang held the pass west, Zhao held Bing Province, Zhongyuan held Dong Commandery — each amassed troops and acted as tyrants, and the realm suffered bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong, Dulü, and Yanbo held the court; Tianguang held the west, Zhao held Bing Province, and Zhongyuan held Dong Commandery—each tyrannized with armed force, and all under heaven groaned.

sentences.zh: 葛榮衆流入幷、肆者二十餘萬，為契胡陵暴，皆不聊生，大小二十六反，誅夷者半，猶草竊不止。

translations.literal: Ge Rong's followers who had flowed into Bing and Si numbered over two hundred thousand; oppressed by the Jie-Hu they could not live, and there were twenty-six uprisings large and small; half were executed, yet scattered pillaging still did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: More than two hundred thousand of Ge Rong's followers had drifted into Bing and Si; bullied by the Jie-Hu, they could scarcely survive. There were twenty-six rebellions, large and small; half the rebels were killed, yet brigandage never stopped.

sentences.zh: 兆患之，問計於神武。

translations.literal: Zhao was troubled by this and asked Shenwu for a plan.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao was vexed by this and asked Gao Huan's counsel.

sentences.zh: 神武曰：「六鎮反殘，不可盡殺，宜選王素腹心者私使統焉。

translations.literal: Shenwu said: "The rebel remnants of the Six Garrisons cannot all be killed; you should choose men who are by nature close to Your Highness and privately appoint them to command them.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "The Six Garrisons rebels cannot all be slaughtered. Send men you trust in private to command them.

sentences.zh: 若有犯者，直罪其帥，則所罪者寡。

translations.literal: If there are offenders, punish only their commanders, then those punished will be few.
translations.idiomatic: When crimes occur, punish only the commander, and few will suffer.

sentences.zh: 」兆曰：「善，誰可行也？

translations.literal: " Zhao said: "Good — who can undertake this?
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said, "Well said—who should take it?"

sentences.zh: 」賀拔允時在坐，請神武。

translations.literal: Heba Yun was then seated there and recommended Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Yun, who was present, named Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 神武拳毆之，折其一齒，曰：「生平天柱時，奴輩伏處分如鷹犬，今日天下安置在王，而阿鞠泥敢誣下罔上，請殺之。

translations.literal: Shenwu punched and beat him, breaking one tooth, and said: "In the lifetime when the Heavenly Pillar lived, you fellows submitted to orders like hawks and hounds. Today the realm rests under Your Highness's arrangement, yet Ajuni dares falsely accuse subordinates and deceive superiors — I ask that he be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan struck him with his fist and broke a tooth, saying, "In the days of the Heavenly Pillar you crawled to his commands like hunting dogs. The realm now rests with you, my lord, yet this flatterer dares deceive you—I ask leave to kill him.

sentences.zh: 」兆以神武為誠，遂以委焉。

translations.literal: Zhao took Shenwu as sincere and thereupon entrusted it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao took Gao Huan for sincere and entrusted the command to him.

sentences.zh: 神武以兆醉，恐醒後或致疑貳，遂出，宣言受委統州鎮兵，可集汾東受令。

translations.literal: Shenwu, because Zhao was drunk, feared that when sober he might grow suspicious and doubtful; he therefore went out and proclaimed that having received commission to command the garrison troops of the province, they could assemble east of the Fen to receive orders.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhao was drunk, Gao Huan feared he might afterward grow suspicious; he went out and proclaimed that, empowered to command the provincial garrisons, the troops were to assemble east of the Fen for orders.

sentences.zh: 乃建牙陽曲川，陳部分。

translations.literal: He then raised the command banner at Yangqu Stream and set forth the organization.
translations.idiomatic: At Yangqu Stream he raised his headquarters banner and organized his divisions.

sentences.zh: 有款軍門者，絳巾袍，自稱梗楊驛子，願廁左右。

translations.literal: One came to the camp gate in submission wearing a red kerchief robe, calling himself the runner at Gengyang station, wishing to attend at left and right.
translations.idiomatic: A man in a red kerchief and robe came to the gate, calling himself the Gengyang relay runner, and asked to serve at Gao Huan's side.

sentences.zh: 訪之，則以力聞，常於幷州市搭殺人者，乃署為親信。

translations.literal: Inquiring into him, he was known for strength and had often at Bingzhou market killed men in brawls; he was therefore appointed trusted attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Inquiry showed he was famed for strength and had killed men in brawls at the Bingzhou market; Gao Huan made him a personal guard.

sentences.zh: 兵士素惡兆而樂神武，於是莫不皆至。

translations.literal: The soldiers had long hated Zhao and delighted in Shenwu; hence none failed to come.
translations.idiomatic: The troops had long hated Erzhu Zhao and welcomed Gao Huan, so all rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 居無何，又使劉貴請兆，以幷、肆頻歲霜旱，降戶掘黃鼠而食之，皆面無穀色，徒汚人國土，請令就食山東，待溫飽而處分之。

translations.literal: Before long, he again had Liu Gui ask Zhao, saying that Bing and Si had suffered frost and drought year after year, the surrendered households dug yellow rats to eat, all without grain color in their faces, merely fouling the realm's soil in vain — he asked that they be allowed to forage in Shandong and, once warm and fed, be settled and disposed of.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Gao Huan sent Liu Gui to ask Zhao: Bing and Si had suffered frost and drought for years; surrendered households dug out yellow rats to eat, faces gaunt and wasted. Let them move east to forage in Shandong and settle once they are fed, he urged.

sentences.zh: 兆從其議。

translations.literal: Zhao followed this proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao agreed.

sentences.zh: 其長史慕容紹宗諫曰：「不可，今四方擾擾，人懷異望，況高公雄略，又握大兵，將不可為。

translations.literal: His chief clerk Murong Shaozong remonstrated, saying: "It must not be done. Now the four quarters are in turmoil and men harbor divergent hopes; moreover High Duke Gao is heroic in strategy and holds great armies — this will not do.
translations.idiomatic: His chief secretary Murong Shaozong warned, "You cannot do this. The realm is in turmoil and men turn their hopes elsewhere; Gao Huan is ambitious and now commands a great army—this cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 」兆曰：「香火重誓，何所慮也。

translations.literal: " Zhao said: "We have sworn a solemn oath before the incense — what is there to worry about?
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said, "We swore a blood oath at the incense altar—what is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 」紹宗曰：「親兄弟尚爾難信，何論香火！

translations.literal: Shaozong said: "Even full brothers are thus hard to trust — how much less an oath before incense!
translations.idiomatic: Shaozong replied, "Full brothers cannot trust each other—what use is a sworn oath?"

sentences.zh: 」時兆左右已受神武金，因譖紹宗與神武舊有隙，兆乃禁紹宗而催神武發。

translations.literal: At that time those at Zhao's side had already received Shenwu's gold; they therefore slandered Shaozong, saying he and Shenwu had old grudges; Zhao thereupon confined Shaozong and urged Shenwu to depart.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhao's attendants had taken Gao Huan's gold and accused Shaozong of an old feud with Gao Huan; Zhao imprisoned Shaozong and pressed Gao Huan to march.

sentences.zh: 神武乃自晉陽出滏口。

translations.literal: Shenwu then departed Jinyang through Fukou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan marched out of Jinyang through Fukou Pass.

sentences.zh: 路逢尒朱榮妻北鄉長公主，自洛陽來，馬三百匹，盡奪易之。

translations.literal: On the road he met the Northern Xiangchang Princess, wife of Erzhu Rong, coming from Luoyang with three hundred horses; he seized them all and exchanged for them.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he met the Northern Xiangchang Princess, Erzhu Rong's widow, riding from Luoyang with three hundred horses—and seized every one.

sentences.zh: 兆聞，乃釋紹宗而問焉。

translations.literal: When Zhao heard, he released Shaozong and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao heard, he released Shaozong and asked his meaning.

sentences.zh: 紹宗曰：「猶掌握中物也。

translations.literal: Shaozong said: "It is still like something in the palm of the hand.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozong said, "It is still something clasped in your palm.

sentences.zh: 」於是自追神武。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he himself pursued Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: He set out in pursuit himself.

sentences.zh: 至襄垣，會漳水暴長，橋壞。

translations.literal: Reaching Xiangyuan, the Zhang River suddenly rose in flood and the bridge was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangyuan the Zhang River had swollen and broken the bridge.

sentences.zh: 神武隔水拜曰：「所以借公主馬，非有他故，備山東盜耳。

translations.literal: Shenwu bowed across the water and said: "The reason I borrowed the princess's horses was for no other cause — only to guard against bandits in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan bowed from across the water and said, "I took the princess's horses only to provision against bandits in the east.

sentences.zh: 王受公主言，自來賜追，今渡河而死不辭，此衆便叛。

translations.literal: Your Highness, having received the princess's words, came yourself in pursuit — if I cross the river now and die I will not refuse, but these troops will at once rebel.
translations.idiomatic: You came because of her complaint—but if I ford the river now and die, I will not refuse; this army will rebel.

sentences.zh: 」兆自陳無此意，因輕馬渡，與神武坐幕下，陳謝，遂授刀引頭，使神武斫己。

translations.literal: " Zhao himself declared he had no such intent; thereupon he crossed lightly on horseback, sat with Shenwu under the tent, stated his apology, then handed over a knife and offered his neck, allowing Shenwu to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao swore he meant no harm, rode across lightly, and sat with Gao Huan under the tent to apologize; he handed over a knife and offered his neck for Gao Huan to strike.

sentences.zh: 神武大哭曰：「自天柱薨背，賀六渾更何所仰，願大家千萬歲，以申力用。

translations.literal: Shenwu wept greatly and said: "Since the Heavenly Pillar passed away, on what does Heiliuhun anymore rely? I wish Your Lordship ten thousand years, that my strength may be employed.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan wept and said, "Since the Heavenly Pillar died, Heiliuhun has no one else to serve. Live ten thousand years, my lord, that I may still put my strength at your use.

sentences.zh: 今旁人構間至此，大家何忍復出此言！

translations.literal: Now others have built estrangement to this point — how can Your Lordship bear to speak thus again!
translations.idiomatic: Others have driven this wedge between us—how can you speak so again!

sentences.zh: 」兆投刀於地，遂刑白馬而盟，誓為兄弟，留宿夜飲。

translations.literal: " Zhao threw the knife to the ground; they thereupon slaughtered a white horse and swore alliance, vowing brotherhood, and stayed the night drinking.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao cast the knife aside; they sacrificed a white horse and swore brotherhood again, staying up drinking through the night.

sentences.zh: 尉景伏壯士欲執兆，神武齧臂止之曰：「今殺之，其黨必奔歸聚結。

translations.literal: Jing concealed strong men intending to seize Zhao; Shenwu bit his arm to stop him, saying: "If we kill him now, his faction will surely flee and gather to reassemble.
translations.idiomatic: Jing had hidden strong men ready to seize Zhao; Gao Huan bit his arm to stop him, saying, "Kill him now and his faction will scatter and regroup.

sentences.zh: 兵饑馬瘦，不可相支，若英雄崛起，則為害滋甚。

translations.literal: The troops are hungry and the horses lean; we cannot sustain one another; if heroes rise up, the harm will be all the greater.
translations.idiomatic: Our troops are hungry and our horses spent—we cannot afford a split. If some hero rises, the harm will be worse.

sentences.zh: 不如且置之。

translations.literal: Better for now to let him go.
translations.idiomatic: Better to leave him be for now.

sentences.zh: 兆雖勁捷，而凶狡無謀，不足圖也。

translations.literal: Although Zhao is vigorous and swift, he is fierce, cunning, and without strategy — not worth contriving against.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao is fierce but witless—not worth plotting against.

sentences.zh: 」旦日，兆歸營，又召神武，神武將上馬詣之，孫騰牽衣，乃止。

translations.literal: " Next day Zhao returned to camp and again summoned Shenwu; Shenwu was about to mount his horse and go to him, but Sun Teng held his robe and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Zhao returned to camp and summoned Gao Huan again; Gao Huan was about to ride to him, but Sun Teng seized his robe and held him back.

sentences.zh: 兆隔水肆罵，馳還晉陽。

translations.literal: Zhao railed wantonly across the water and galloped back to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao cursed him from across the river and galloped back to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 兆心腹念賢領降戶家累別為營，神武偽與之善，觀其佩刀，因取之以殺其從者，從者盡散。

translations.literal: Zhao's trusted man Nianxian led the families of surrendered households in a separate encampment; Shenwu feigned friendship with him, observed the blade he wore at his belt, and took it to kill his followers; the followers all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Nianxian, a trusted man of Zhao's, camped apart with the families of surrendered households; Gao Huan feigned friendship, snatched the blade at his belt, and killed his escort—the rest scattered.

sentences.zh: 於是士衆咸悅，倍願附從。

translations.literal: Thereupon officers and troops were all pleased and doubly wished to attach themselves and follow.
translations.idiomatic: The army rejoiced and rallied to him in greater numbers.

sentences.zh: 初，魏真君內學者奏言上黨有天子氣，云在壺關大王山。

translations.literal: Initially, inner-learning scholars under Wei Emperor Taiwu memorialized that Shangdang had the qi of a Son of Heaven, saying it was at Dawang Mountain in Huguan.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Taiwu's day, court scholars reported that Shangdang bore the aura of an emperor—at Dawang Mountain in Huguan.

sentences.zh: 太武帝於是南巡以厭當之，累石為三封，斬其北鳳凰山，以毀其形。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu thereupon toured south to suppress and counter it, piled stones into three mounds, and cut down the northern Fenghuang Mountain to destroy its form.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu marched south to suppress it, piled stones into three cairns, and cut down Northern Fenghuang Mountain to break its form.

sentences.zh: 後上黨人居晉陽者，號上黨坊，神武實居之。

translations.literal: Later those from Shangdang living at Jinyang were called Shangdang Ward; Shenwu actually dwelled there.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Shangdang exiles at Jinyang lived in what was called Shangdang Ward—and Gao Huan had lived there.

sentences.zh: 及是行，舍大王山六旬而進。

translations.literal: On this march he lodged at Dawang Mountain sixty days before advancing.
translations.idiomatic: On this march he camped at Dawang Mountain for sixty days before advancing.

sentences.zh: 將出滏口，倍加約束，纖毫之物，不聽侵犯。

translations.literal: About to exit Fukou, he doubly tightened discipline; not the slightest item was permitted to be plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving Fukou he tightened discipline sharply—not the smallest thing might be taken.

sentences.zh: 將過麥地，神武輒步牽馬。

translations.literal: About to pass through wheat fields, Shenwu always walked leading his horse.
translations.idiomatic: Passing wheat fields, he always led his horse on foot.

sentences.zh: 遠近聞之，皆稱高儀同將兵整肅，歸心焉。

translations.literal: Near and far hearing of it, all praised Commandant Gao for leading troops with stern order, and turned their hearts to him.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far men praised Commandant Gao for his disciplined troops and gave him their hearts.

sentences.zh: 遂前行，屯鄴，求糧相州刺史劉誕，誕不供。

translations.literal: He then advanced, encamped at Ye, and sought grain from Liu Dan, governor of Xiang Province; Dan did not supply it.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on and encamped at Ye, but Liu Dan, governor of Xiang Province, refused him grain.

sentences.zh: 有軍營租米，神武自取之。

translations.literal: There was rent rice at a military camp; Shenwu took it himself.
translations.idiomatic: He took it himself from the military storehouses.

sentences.zh: 魏普泰元年二月，神武自軍次信都，高乾、封隆之開門以待，遂據冀州。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Putai of Wei, Shenwu's army halted at Xindu; Gao Gan and Feng Longzhi opened the gates to await him, and he thereupon seized Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Wei Putai 1 (531), Gao Huan halted at Xindu; Gao Gan and Feng Longzhi opened the gates, and he seized Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 是月，尒朱度律廢元曄而立節閔帝，欲羈縻神武。

translations.literal: That month Erzhu Dulü deposed Yuan Ye and enthroned Emperor Jiemin, intending to restrain and attach Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: That month Erzhu Dulü deposed Yuan Ye and enthroned Emperor Jiemin, hoping to bind Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 三月，乃白節閔帝，封神武為渤海王，徵使入覲。

translations.literal: In the third month he reported to Emperor Jiemin, enfeoffed Shenwu as Prince of Bohai, and summoned him to court audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he had Emperor Jiemin enfeoff Gao Huan as Prince of Bohai and summoned him to court.

sentences.zh: 神武辭。

translations.literal: Shenwu declined.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan declined.

sentences.zh: 四月癸巳，又加授東道大行臺、第一鎮人酋長。

translations.literal: On the guisi day of the fourth month, he was further granted Eastern Route Grand Chief and First Chief of the Garrison Peoples.
translations.idiomatic: On the guisi day of the fourth month he was further given Eastern Route Grand Chief and First Chief of the Garrison Peoples.

sentences.zh: 龐蒼鷹自太原來奔，神武以為行臺郎，尋以為安州刺史。

translations.literal: Pang Cangying came fleeing from Taiyuan; Shenwu made him a clerk on the chief's staff, and soon after made him governor of An Province.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Cangying fled from Taiyuan; Gao Huan made him a chief's clerk, then governor of An Province.

sentences.zh: 神武自向山東，養士繕甲，禁侵掠，百姓歸心。

translations.literal: Shenwu himself turned toward Shandong, nurtured soldiers and repaired armor, forbade pillaging, and the common people turned their hearts to him.
translations.idiomatic: Turning east into Shandong, Gao Huan drilled troops and repaired armor, forbade pillaging, and won the people.

sentences.zh: 乃詐為書，言尒朱兆將以六鎮人配契胡為部曲，衆皆愁怨。

translations.literal: He then forged a letter saying Erzhu Zhao would assign the Six Garrisons men to the Jie-Hu as retainers; the multitude all groaned with resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He forged a letter claiming Erzhu Zhao would assign the Six Garrisons men to the Jie-Hu as retainers, and the army groaned with anger.

sentences.zh: 又為幷州符，徵兵討步落稽。

translations.literal: He again forged an order from Bing Province, conscripting troops to campaign against the Buluoji.
translations.idiomatic: He also forged a Bingzhou conscription order to fight the Buluoji.

sentences.zh: 發萬人，將遣之，孫騰、尉景為請留五日，如此者再。

translations.literal: He mobilized ten thousand men and was about to send them off; Sun Teng and Jing asked that they be kept five days — twice thus.
translations.idiomatic: He called up ten thousand men to send away; Sun Teng and Jing twice asked for a five-day delay.

sentences.zh: 神武親送之郊，雪涕執別，人皆號慟，哭聲動地。

translations.literal: Shenwu personally escorted them to the suburbs, weeping as he clasped them in farewell; all wailed and lamented, the sound of crying shaking the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan escorted them to the suburbs himself, weeping as he took leave; the men wailed until the earth seemed to shake.

sentences.zh: 神武乃喻之曰：「與爾俱失鄉客，義同一家，不意在上乃爾徵召。

translations.literal: Shenwu then explained to them: "I with you all lost our native places as sojourners; in duty we are one family — I did not expect those above would summon you thus.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan told them, "We are all exiles from home, one family in name—I never thought they would summon you like this.

sentences.zh: 直向西已當死，後軍期又當死，配國人又當死，奈何！

translations.literal: Go straight west and you should die; fail the army deadline and again you should die; be assigned to the country's people and again you should die — what is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: March west and you die; miss the deadline and you die; be handed to the Jie-Hu and you die—what can we do?

sentences.zh: 」衆曰：「唯有反耳！

translations.literal: " The multitude said: "Only rebellion remains!
translations.idiomatic: The men cried, "We can only rebel!"

sentences.zh: 」神武曰：「反是急計，須推一人為主。

translations.literal: " Shenwu said: "Rebellion is the urgent plan; we must choose one man as leader.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "Rebellion is the urgent move—but we must choose a leader.

sentences.zh: 」衆願奉神武。

translations.literal: The multitude wished to uphold Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: They wanted Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 神武曰：「爾鄉里難制，不見葛榮乎？

translations.literal: Shenwu said: "Your fellow-townsmen are hard to control — have you not seen Ge Rong?
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "Your kind is hard to rule—have you forgotten Ge Rong?

sentences.zh: 雖百萬衆，無刑法，終自灰滅。

translations.literal: Though he had a million followers, without law and punishment he in the end perished to ash and extinction.
translations.idiomatic: A million men, and without law he perished to nothing.

sentences.zh: 今以吾為主，當與前異，不得欺漢兒，不得犯軍令，生死任吾則可，不爾不能為，取笑天下。

translations.literal: Now taking me as leader, it must differ from before — you must not cheat the Han subjects, must not violate army commands; if life and death are entrusted to me then it can be done, otherwise it cannot be done, becoming the laughingstock of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Make me your leader and things will differ: no cheating Han subjects, no breaking army law. Give me your lives and I will lead you—or leave and be mocked by the realm.

sentences.zh: 」衆皆頓顙，死生唯命。

translations.literal: The multitude all prostrated their foreheads; life and death were as he commanded.
translations.idiomatic: They bowed to the ground and pledged their lives to his command.

sentences.zh: 神武曰若不得已。

translations.literal: Shenwu said, if there is no other way.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "If there is no other way."

sentences.zh: 明日，椎牛饗士，喻以討尒朱之意。

translations.literal: Next day he slaughtered an ox to feast the troops and explained the intent to campaign against the Erzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he slaughtered an ox to feast the troops and declared war on the Erzhu.

sentences.zh: 封隆之進曰：「千載一時，普天幸甚。

translations.literal: Feng Longzhi came forward and said: "A moment once in a thousand years — all under heaven is greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Longzhi came forward and said, "A moment that comes once in a thousand years—all heaven is fortunate.

sentences.zh: 」神武曰：「討賊，大順也；

translations.literal: " Shenwu said: "Punishing the rebels is great accord with righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "Punishing these rebels is righteousness itself;

sentences.zh: 拯時，大業也。

translations.literal: succoring the age is great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: saving the age is great endeavor.

sentences.zh: 吾雖不武，以死繼之，何敢讓焉！」

translations.literal: Though I am not martial, to follow with my death — how would I dare yield!
translations.idiomatic: I am no warrior, but I will follow with my life—how could I refuse!"

sentences.zh: 六月庚子，建義於信都，尚未顯背尒朱氏。

translations.literal: On the gengzi day of the sixth month he raised righteousness at Xindu, not yet openly turning against the Erzhu house.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day of the sixth month he raised the banner at Xindu, not yet openly breaking with the Erzhu.

sentences.zh: 及李元忠與高乾平殷州，斬尒朱羽生首來謁，神武撫膺曰：「今日反決矣。

translations.literal: When Li Yuanzhong with Gao Gan pacified Yin Province and beheaded Erzhu Yusheng, coming to pay respects, Shenwu beat his breast and said: "Today rebellion is decided.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yuanzhong and Gao Gan took Yin Province and brought Erzhu Yusheng's head, Gao Huan struck his breast and said, "Today the break is made.

sentences.zh: 」乃以元忠為殷州刺史。

translations.literal: " He thereupon made Yuanzhong governor of Yin Province.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Yuanzhong governor of Yin Province.

sentences.zh: 是時兵威旣振，乃抗表罪狀尒朱氏。

translations.literal: At this time military might was already aroused; he thereupon submitted a memorial listing the Erzhu house's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: His army's strength now shown, he submitted a memorial denouncing the Erzhu clan.

sentences.zh: 世隆等秘表不通。

translations.literal: Shilong and the others kept the memorial secret and did not transmit it.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong and the rest suppressed the memorial and never forwarded it.

sentences.zh: 八月，尒朱兆攻陷殷州，李元忠來奔。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Erzhu Zhao captured and overran Yin Province; Li Yuanzhong came fleeing to join him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Erzhu Zhao took Yin Province and Li Yuanzhong fled to Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 孫騰以為朝廷隔絕，不權立天子，則衆望無所系。

translations.literal: Sun Teng held that with the court cut off and isolated, if they did not provisionally establish a Son of Heaven, then the multitude's expectations would have nothing to attach to.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng argued that with the court cut off, only a provisional emperor could hold men's hopes.

sentences.zh: 十月壬寅，奉章武王融子渤海太守朗為皇帝，年號中興，是為廢帝。

translations.literal: On the renyin day of the tenth month they upheld Prince Lang, son of Prince Zhangwu Rong and Bohai governor, as emperor, era name Zhongxing — this was the Deposed Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day of the tenth month they enthroned Lang, son of Prince Zhangwu Rong and governor of Bohai, as emperor under the era Zhongxing—the later Deposed Emperor.

sentences.zh: 時度律、仲遠軍次陽平，尒朱兆會之。

translations.literal: At that time Dulü and Zhongyuan's armies halted at Yangping; Erzhu Zhao joined them.
translations.idiomatic: Dulü and Zhongyuan halted at Yangping, and Erzhu Zhao joined them.

sentences.zh: 神武用竇泰策，縱反間，度律、仲遠不戰而還。

translations.literal: Shenwu used Dou Tai's stratagem, set loose counter-intelligence; Dulü and Zhongyuan returned without battle.
translations.idiomatic: Using Dou Tai's counsel, Gao Huan spread discord and Dulü and Zhongyuan withdrew without fighting.

sentences.zh: 神武乃敗兆於廣阿。

translations.literal: Shenwu thereupon defeated Zhao at Guang'a.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan then defeated Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a.

sentences.zh: 十一月，攻鄴，相州刺史劉誕嬰城固守。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he attacked Ye; Liu Dan, governor of Xiang Province, closed the city and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he attacked Ye; Liu Dan, governor of Xiang Province, barred the gates and held firm.

sentences.zh: 神武起土山，為地道，往往建大柱，一時焚之，城陷入地。

translations.literal: Shenwu raised earth mounds, dug tunnels, and in places erected great pillars; at one stroke he burned them, and the wall sank into the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan built earthworks and dug tunnels, propping them with great pillars that he burned at once—the walls collapsed into the earth.

sentences.zh: 麻祥時為湯陰令，神武呼之曰：「麻都！

translations.literal: Ma Xiang was then magistrate of Tangyin; Shenwu called to him: "Prefect Ma!
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xiang was magistrate of Tangyin; Gao Huan called out, "Prefect Ma!

sentences.zh: 」祥慚而逃。

translations.literal: " Xiang, ashamed, fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, Xiang fled.

sentences.zh: 永熙元年正月壬午，拔鄴城，據之。

translations.literal: On the renwu day of the first month of the first year of Yongxi, he captured Ye city and held it.
translations.idiomatic: On the renwu day of the first month of Yongxi 1 (532), he took Ye and held it.

sentences.zh: 廢帝進神武大丞相、柱國大將軍、太師。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor advanced Shenwu to Grand Chancellor, Pillar-of-State Grand General, and Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor promoted Gao Huan to Grand Chancellor, Pillar-of-State Grand General, and Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 是時青州建義，大都督崔靈珍、大都督耿翔皆遣使歸附。

translations.literal: At this time righteousness was raised in Qing Province; Grand Commander Cui Lingzhen and Grand Commander Geng Xiang both sent envoys to submit and attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Qing Province rose in rebellion; Grand Commanders Cui Lingzhen and Geng Xiang both sent envoys to submit.

sentences.zh: 行汾州事劉貴棄城來降。

translations.literal: Liu Gui, acting for Fen Province, abandoned the city and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gui, who was administering Fen Province, abandoned his post and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 閏三月，尒朱天光自長安、兆自幷州、度律自洛陽、仲遠自東郡同會鄴，衆號二十萬，挾洹水而軍，節閔以長孫承業為大行臺總督焉。

translations.literal: In the intercalary third month, Erzhu Tianguang from Chang'an, Zhao from Bing Province, Dulü from Luoyang, and Zhongyuan from Dong Commandery all assembled at Ye; the host was said to number two hundred thousand. They camped along the Huan River. Emperor Jiemin put Changsun Chengye in charge as Grand Chief of the Eastern Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary third month Erzhu Tianguang marched from Chang'an, Zhao from Bing Province, Dulü from Luoyang, and Zhongyuan from Dong Commandery to meet at Ye with a force said to number two hundred thousand. They camped along the Huan River while Emperor Jiemin put Changsun Chengye in overall command as Grand Eastern Chief.

sentences.zh: 神武令封隆之守鄴，自出頓紫陌。

translations.literal: Shenwu ordered Feng Longzhi to hold Ye and marched out himself to encamp at Zimo.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan left Feng Longzhi to hold Ye and marched out to encamp at Zimo.

sentences.zh: 時馬不滿二千，步兵不至三萬，衆寡不敵。

translations.literal: At the time cavalry did not reach two thousand and infantry not thirty thousand — the many and the few could not match.
translations.idiomatic: He had fewer than two thousand horse and not thirty thousand foot—the odds were impossible.

sentences.zh: 乃於韓陵為圓陣，連牛驢以塞歸道，於是將士皆有死志，四面赴擊之。

translations.literal: Thereupon at Hanling he formed a circular array, linking oxen and donkeys to block the return road; the officers and troops all had the will to die, and struck them from four sides.
translations.idiomatic: At Hanling he formed a ring formation and chained oxen and donkeys to block retreat. Officers and men alike resolved to die, then struck from every side.

sentences.zh: 尒朱兆責神武以背己，神武曰：「本戮力者，共輔王室，今帝何在？

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhao blamed Shenwu for turning against him. Shenwu said: "We joined forces to support the royal house — where is the emperor now?
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao accused Gao Huan of betrayal. Gao Huan said, "We joined forces to serve the throne—where is the emperor now?

sentences.zh: 」兆曰：「永安枉害天柱，我報讐耳。

translations.literal: " Zhao said: "Yong'an wrongly killed the Heavenly Pillar; I am only avenging him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said, "Emperor Yong'an wrongly killed the Heavenly Pillar. I am only avenging him.

sentences.zh: 」神武曰：「我昔日親聞天柱計，汝在戶前立，豈得言不反邪？

translations.literal: " Shenwu said: "I personally heard the Heavenly Pillar's plan in former days — you stood before the gate. How can you say you did not mean to rebel?
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "I heard the Heavenly Pillar's plan myself—you stood at the gate. Can you say you never meant to rebel?

sentences.zh: 且以君殺臣，何報之有？

translations.literal: Moreover, when a lord kills his minister, what vengeance is owed?
translations.idiomatic: When a lord kills his minister, what vengeance is owed?

sentences.zh: 今日義絕矣。

translations.literal: Today righteousness is severed.
translations.idiomatic: Today our bond of righteousness is broken.

sentences.zh: 」乃合戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they joined battle and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: They joined battle and routed him utterly.

sentences.zh: 尒朱兆對慕容紹宗叩心曰：「不用公言，以至於此！

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhao clutched his chest before Murong Shaozong and said: "Had I heeded you, it would not have come to this!
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao clutched his chest before Murong Shaozong and cried, "Had I listened to you, this would never have happened!

sentences.zh: 」將輕走。

translations.literal: " He was about to flee lightly.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to flee with a light escort.

sentences.zh: 紹宗反旗鳴角，收聚散卒，成軍容而西上。

translations.literal: Shaozong turned the banners and sounded the horns, gathered the scattered troops, restored military order, and marched west.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozong reversed the banners and sounded the horns, rallied the scattered troops, restored order, and marched west.

sentences.zh: 高季式以七騎追奔，度野馬崗，與兆遇。

translations.literal: Gao Jishi pursued the rout with seven horsemen, crossed Yema Ridge, and met Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jishi pursued with seven riders, crossed Yema Ridge, and met Zhao.

sentences.zh: 高昂望之不見，哭曰：「喪吾弟矣！

translations.literal: Gao Ao looked and did not see him; he wept and said: "I have lost my brother!
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ao looked and could not see him; he wept and said, "I have lost my brother!

sentences.zh: 」夜久，季式還，血滿袖。

translations.literal: " Late at night Jishi returned, his sleeves drenched in blood.
translations.idiomatic: Late that night Jishi returned, his sleeves drenched in blood.

sentences.zh: 斛斯椿倍道先據河橋。

translations.literal: Husi Chun raced by forced marches and seized the River Bridge first.
translations.idiomatic: Husi Chun raced ahead by forced marches and seized the River Bridge first.

sentences.zh: 初，普泰元年十月，歲星、熒惑、鎮星、太白聚於觜，參色甚明。

translations.literal: Initially, in the tenth month of the first year of Putai, Jupiter, Mars, Saturn, and Venus gathered at Zi and Shen — their light was very bright.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the tenth month of Wei Putai 1 (531), Jupiter, Mars, Saturn, and Venus gathered at Zi and Shen, shining with unusual brilliance.

sentences.zh: 太史占云當有王者興。

translations.literal: The court astronomers divined that a true king would rise.
translations.idiomatic: The court astronomers divined that a true king would rise.

sentences.zh: 是時神武起於信都，至是而破兆等。

translations.literal: At that time Shenwu had risen at Xindu; by now he had broken Zhao and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan had risen at Xindu—and by now he had broken Zhao and the rest.

sentences.zh: 四月，斛斯椿執天光、度律送洛陽。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Husi Chun seized Tianguang and Dulü and sent them to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Husi Chun seized Tianguang and Dulü and sent them to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 長孫承業遣都督賈顯智、張歡入洛陽，執世隆、彥伯斬之。

translations.literal: Changsun Chengye sent commanders Jia Xianzhi and Zhang Huan into Luoyang to seize Shilong and Yanbo and behead them.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Chengye sent commanders Jia Xianzhi and Zhang Huan into Luoyang to seize Shilong and Yanbo and behead them.

sentences.zh: 兆奔幷州。

translations.literal: Zhao fled to Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao fled to Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 仲遠奔梁州，遂死焉。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan fled to Liang Province and there died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan fled to Liang Province and died there.

sentences.zh: 時凶蠹旣除，朝廷慶悅。

translations.literal: At that time, with the wicked eliminated, the court rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: With the wicked eliminated, the court rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 初，未戰之前月，章武人張紹夜中忽被數騎將踰城，至一大將軍前，敕紹為軍導向鄴，云佐受命者除殘賊。

translations.literal: Initially, in the month before the battle, Zhang Shao of Zhangwu was suddenly seized at night by several horsemen who carried him over the wall to a great general. He was ordered to guide the army toward Ye, it being said that one who had received Heaven's mandate would aid in destroying the wicked.
translations.idiomatic: Before the battle, in the month prior, Zhang Shao of Zhangwu was seized at night by several horsemen who carried him over the wall to a great general. He was ordered to guide the army toward Ye for one who had received Heaven's mandate to destroy the wicked.

sentences.zh: 紹迴視之，兵不測，整疾無聲。

translations.literal: Shao looked back — the troops could not be counted; they marched in perfect order without a sound.
translations.idiomatic: Shao looked back—the host was beyond counting, marching in perfect silence.

sentences.zh: 將至鄴，乃放焉。

translations.literal: When they were about to reach Ye, they released him.
translations.idiomatic: Nearing Ye, they released him.

sentences.zh: 及戰之日，尒朱氏軍人見陣外士馬四合，蓋神助也。

translations.literal: On the day of battle the Erzhu soldiers saw horsemen closing in from every side of the formation — Heaven's aid, it was said.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of battle Erzhu soldiers saw horsemen closing in from every side of the field—Heaven's aid, men said.

sentences.zh: 旣而神武至洛陽，廢節閔及中興主而立孝武。

translations.literal: Soon Shenwu reached Luoyang, deposed Emperor Jiemin and the Zhongxing ruler, and enthroned Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Gao Huan reached Luoyang, deposed Emperor Jiemin and the Zhongxing emperor, and enthroned Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 孝武旣卽位，授神武大丞相、天柱大將軍、太師、世襲定州刺史，增封並前十五萬戶。

translations.literal: Once Xiaowu had taken the throne, he appointed Shenwu Grand Chancellor, Pillar-of-State Grand General, Grand Preceptor, and hereditary governor of Ding Province, raising his fief together with previous grants to one hundred fifty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned, Emperor Xiaowu made Gao Huan Grand Chancellor, Pillar-of-State Grand General, Grand Preceptor, and hereditary governor of Ding Province, raising his fief to one hundred fifty thousand households in all.

sentences.zh: 神武辭天柱，減戶五萬。

translations.literal: Shenwu declined the Pillar-of-State title and surrendered fifty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan declined the Pillar-of-State title and surrendered fifty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，還鄴，魏帝餞於乾脯山，執手而別。

translations.literal: On the renchen day he returned to Ye; the Wei emperor saw him off at Ganfu Mountain, clasping hands in farewell.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day he returned to Ye; the Wei emperor saw him off at Ganfu Mountain, clasping hands in parting.

sentences.zh: 七月壬寅，神武帥師北伐尒朱兆。

translations.literal: On the renyin day of the seventh month Shenwu led his army north to campaign against Erzhu Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day of the seventh month Gao Huan led his army north against Erzhu Zhao.

sentences.zh: 封隆之言：「侍中斛斯椿、賀拔勝、賈顯智等往事尒朱，普皆反噬，今在京師，寵任，必構禍隙。

translations.literal: Feng Longzhi said: "Palace Attendants Husi Chun, Helü Sheng, and Jia Xianzhi once served the Erzhu — all turned and bit their masters. Now in the capital, favored and trusted, they will surely sow the seeds of disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Longzhi said, "Palace Attendants Husi Chun, Helü Sheng, and Jia Xianzhi once served the Erzhu and all turned on their masters. Now favored in the capital, they will surely sow discord.

sentences.zh: 」神武深以為然，乃歸天光、度律於京師，斬之。

translations.literal: " Shenwu took this deeply to heart and sent Tianguang and Dulü back to the capital to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan took this to heart and sent Tianguang and Dulü back to the capital to be executed.

sentences.zh: 遂自滏口入。

translations.literal: He thereupon entered by Fekou Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He then entered through Fekou Pass.

sentences.zh: 尒朱兆大掠晉陽，北保秀容。

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhao plundered Jinyang heavily and retreated north to hold Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao plundered Jinyang and retreated north to hold Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 幷州平。

translations.literal: Bing Province was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Province was pacified.

sentences.zh: 神武以晉陽四塞，乃建大丞相府而定居焉。

translations.literal: Shenwu, because Jinyang was blocked on four sides, built the Grand Chancellor's headquarters there and settled.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jinyang was walled in on four sides, Gao Huan built his Grand Chancellor's headquarters there and made it his base.

sentences.zh: 尒朱兆旣至秀容，分兵守險，出入寇抄。

translations.literal: Once Erzhu Zhao had reached Xiurong, he split his forces to hold the passes and raided in and out.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiurong Zhao split his forces to hold the passes and raided back and forth.

sentences.zh: 神武揚聲討之，師出止者數四，兆意怠。

translations.literal: Shenwu loudly proclaimed he would attack; his army marched out only to halt — four times this happened — and Zhao grew slack.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan loudly proclaimed he would attack, yet his army marched out and halted four times, until Zhao grew careless.

sentences.zh: 神武揣其歲首當宴會，遣竇泰以精騎馳之，一日一夜行三百里，神武以大軍繼之。

translations.literal: Shenwu guessed that at the New Year Zhao would be feasting; he sent Dou Tai with elite cavalry at a gallop — three hundred li in one day and one night — and followed with the main army.
translations.idiomatic: Guessing Zhao would be feasting at the New Year, Gao Huan sent Dou Tai with elite cavalry at a gallop—three hundred li in a day and a night—and followed with the main army.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，竇泰奄至尒朱兆庭。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year Dou Tai suddenly arrived at Erzhu Zhao's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year Dou Tai suddenly arrived at Erzhu Zhao's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 軍人因宴休惰，忽見泰軍，驚走。

translations.literal: The troops, drunk and idle from feasting, suddenly saw Dou Tai's army and fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were drunk and idle from feasting; seeing Dou Tai's army they fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 追破之於赤洪嶺。

translations.literal: He pursued and broke them at Chihong Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued and broke them at Chihong Ridge.

sentences.zh: 兆自縊，神武親臨厚葬之。

translations.literal: Zhao hanged himself; Shenwu came in person and gave him a lavish burial.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao hanged himself; Gao Huan came in person and gave him a lavish burial.

sentences.zh: 慕容紹宗以尒朱榮妻子及餘衆自保烏突城，降，神武以義故，待之甚厚。

translations.literal: Murong Shaozong held Wutu City with Erzhu Rong's wife and children and the remaining troops; he surrendered, and for old righteousness's sake Shenwu treated him with great generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Shaozong held Wutu City with Erzhu Rong's family and the remnants; he surrendered, and for old righteousness's sake Gao Huan treated him with great generosity.

sentences.zh: 神武之入洛也，尒朱仲遠部下都督橋甯、張子期自滑臺歸命，神武以其助亂，且數反覆，皆斬之。

translations.literal: When Shenwu entered Luoyang, commanders Qiao Ning and Zhang Ziqi of Erzhu Zhongyuan's force submitted from Huatai. Shenwu beheaded them both for aiding rebellion and for repeated treachery.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan entered Luoyang, commanders Qiao Ning and Zhang Ziqi of Erzhu Zhongyuan's force submitted from Huatai. Gao Huan beheaded them for aiding rebellion and for repeated treachery.

sentences.zh: 斛斯椿由是內不自安，乃與南陽王寶炬及武衛將軍元毗、魏光、王思政構神武於魏帝。

translations.literal: Husi Chun was inwardly ill at ease from this; with Prince Nanyang Baoqu and Military Guard Generals Yuan Pi, Wei Guang, and Wang Sizheng he slandered Shenwu to the Wei emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Husi Chun was inwardly ill at ease; with Prince Nanyang Baoqu and Military Guard Generals Yuan Pi, Wei Guang, and Wang Sizheng he slandered Gao Huan to the Wei emperor.

sentences.zh: 舍人元士弼又奏神武受敕大不敬。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Yuan Shibi also memorialized that Shenwu had showed great disrespect in receiving the emperor's edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Yuan Shibi also memorialized that Gao Huan had shown great disrespect in receiving imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 故魏帝心貳於賀拔岳。

translations.literal: Thus the Wei emperor turned his heart toward Helü Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Wei emperor turned his heart toward Helü Yue.

sentences.zh: 初，孝明之時，洛下以兩拔相擊，謠言曰：「銅拔打鐵拔，元家世將末。

translations.literal: Initially, in Emperor Xiaoming's day, Luoyang folk struck two daggers against each other, and a song ran: "Bronze dagger strikes iron dagger — the Yuan clan's great generals will end.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Emperor Xiaoming's day, Luoyang folk struck two daggers together, and a song ran: "Bronze dagger strikes iron dagger—the Yuan clan's great generals will end.

sentences.zh: 」好事者以二拔謂拓拔、賀拔，言俱將衰敗之兆。

translations.literal: " The curious took the two daggers to mean Tuoba and Helü — both clans, they said, were doomed to fall.
translations.idiomatic: The curious took the two daggers to mean Tuoba and Helü—both clans, they said, were doomed to fall.

sentences.zh: 時司空高乾密啟神武，言魏帝之貳，神武封呈。

translations.literal: At that time Minister of Works Gao Qian secretly warned Shenwu that the emperor was divided in heart; Shenwu sealed the letter and forwarded it.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Gao Qian secretly warned Gao Huan that the emperor's heart was divided; Gao Huan sealed the letter and forwarded it.

sentences.zh: 魏帝殺之，又遣東徐州刺史潘紹業密勑長樂太守龐蒼鷹令殺其弟昂。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor had him killed and secretly ordered East Xuzhou governor Pan Shaoye to tell Changle governor Pang Cangying to kill his younger brother Ao.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor had him killed and secretly ordered East Xuzhou governor Pan Shaoye to tell Changle governor Pang Cangying to kill his younger brother Gao Ao.

sentences.zh: 昂先聞其兄死，以矟刺柱，伏壯士執紹業於路，得敕書於袍領，來奔。

translations.literal: Ao had already heard of his brother's death; he drove his spear into a pillar, set strong men to seize Shaoye on the road, found the secret edict in his robe collar, and fled to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Ao had already heard of his brother's death. He drove his spear into a pillar, set strong men to seize Shaoye on the road, found the secret edict in his robe collar, and fled to Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 神武抱其首，哭曰：「天子枉害司空！

translations.literal: Shenwu clasped his head and wept, saying: "The Son of Heaven wrongly killed the Minister of Works!
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan clasped his head and wept, saying, "The Son of Heaven wrongly killed the Minister of Works!

sentences.zh: 」遽使以白武幡勞其家屬。

translations.literal: " He at once sent the white martial banner to condole with his family.
translations.idiomatic: He at once sent the white martial banner to condole with his family.

sentences.zh: 時乾次弟慎在光州，為政嚴猛，又從部下取納，魏帝使代之。

translations.literal: At that time Gao Qian's next-youngest brother Shen was in Guang Province, governing with harsh severity and also taking bribes from his subordinates; the Wei emperor sent someone to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qian's next-youngest brother Shen was in Guang Province, governing with harsh severity and taking bribes from his subordinates; the Wei emperor sent someone to replace him.

sentences.zh: 慎聞難，將奔梁。

translations.literal: Shen heard of the trouble and was about to flee to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen heard of the trouble and was about to flee to Liang.

sentences.zh: 其屬曰：「公家勳重，必不兄弟相及。

translations.literal: His followers said: "Your family's merit is great — they will surely not punish brothers together.
translations.idiomatic: His followers said, "Your family's merit is great—they will surely not punish brothers together.

sentences.zh: 」乃弊衣推鹿車歸渤海。

translations.literal: " He put on shabby clothes, pushed a deer cart, and returned to Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: He put on shabby clothes, pushed a deer cart, and returned to Bohai.

sentences.zh: 逢使者，亦來奔。

translations.literal: He met the imperial envoy on the road and also fled to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He met the imperial envoy on the road and fled to Gao Huan as well.

sentences.zh: 於是魏帝與神武隙矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the breach between the Wei emperor and Shenwu was complete.
translations.idiomatic: The breach between the Wei emperor and Gao Huan was now complete.

sentences.zh: 阿至羅虜正光以前常稱藩，自魏朝多事，皆叛。

translations.literal: The Azhiluo barbarians had regularly paid tribute before Zhengguang; once the Wei court fell into turmoil, they all rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The Azhiluo barbarians had regularly paid tribute before Zhengguang; once the Wei court fell into turmoil, they all rebelled.

sentences.zh: 神武遣使招納，便附款。

translations.literal: Shenwu sent envoys to summon them and they at once submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan sent envoys to summon them and they at once submitted.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔以寇賊平，罷行臺。

translations.literal: Earlier an edict had dissolved the Eastern Headquarters because the rebels were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier an edict had dissolved the Eastern Headquarters because the rebels were pacified.

sentences.zh: 至是，以殊俗歸降，復授神武大行臺，隨機處分。

translations.literal: Now, because distant peoples had submitted, Shenwu was again given the Grand Eastern Headquarters with discretion to act as needed.
translations.idiomatic: Now, because distant peoples had submitted, Gao Huan was again given the Grand Eastern Headquarters with discretion to act as needed.

sentences.zh: 神武常賚其粟帛，議者以為徒費無益，神武不從，撫慰如初。

translations.literal: Shenwu regularly bestowed grain and cloth on them; advisers called it wasted expense, but Shenwu would not listen and continued to comfort them as before.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan regularly bestowed grain and cloth on them; advisers called it wasted expense, but he would not listen and continued to comfort them as before.

sentences.zh: 其酋帥吐陳等感恩，皆從指麾，救曹泥，取万俟受洛干，大收其用。

translations.literal: Their chieftains such as Tuchen were grateful and obeyed every order — rescuing Cao Ni and taking Moqi Shouluogan — and proved of great use.
translations.idiomatic: Their chieftains such as Tuchen were grateful and obeyed every order—rescuing Cao Ni and taking Moqi Shouluogan—proving of great use.

sentences.zh: 河西費也頭虜紇豆陵伊利居河池，恃險擁衆，神武遣長史侯景屢招不從。

translations.literal: The Feiyetou barbarian of Hexi, Qidouling Yili, held Hechi, relying on the terrain and a great following; Shenwu's chief secretary Hou Jing repeatedly summoned him but he would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Feiyetou barbarian of Hexi, Qidouling Yili, held Hechi behind strong terrain with a great following; Gao Huan's chief secretary Hou Jing repeatedly summoned him, but he would not submit.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年十一月、第一版《北齊書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi, November 1972, as the base for collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972).
